item.title: On the average eccentricity of Eulerian and bipartite Eulerian digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.12951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta$. We prove that the average eccentricity of $D$ satisfies $\avec(D) \leq \frac{3n}{\delta+1}$, and that $\avec(D) \leq \frac{2n}{\delta}+2$ if $D$ is bipartite. We show that both bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant and the $\delta+1$ versus $\delta+2$ gap (resp.\ the $\delta$ versus $\delta+1$ gap in the bipartite case), where the average eccentricity of the extremal examples shows that $\avec = \frac{3n}{\delta+2}-2$ in general and $\avec = \frac{2n}{\delta+1}-\frac{5}{2}$ in the bipartite case for $\delta \geq 2$. We further conjecture that these values are the true maxima up to an additive constant (for $\delta \geq 3$ in the bipartite case).
item.dc:creator: Fadekemi Janet Osaye

item.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.13050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.
item.dc:creator: Jens Niklas Eberhardt, Carl Mautner

item.title: Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in the triangular lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.13066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus conjectured that for each non-equilateral triangle $\operatorname{T}$, every 2-coloring of the plane contains a congruent copy of $\operatorname{T}$ with monochromatic vertex set. We confirm this conjecture for triangles with a ratio $\sqrt{7/3}$ between two side lengths. We further prove that every coloring of the plane, regardless of the number of colors used, contains congruent copies of 36 specific triangles with monochromatic or rainbow vertex sets, partially answering a question of Geh\'er, Sagdeev, and T\'oth. Both these results were obtained by considering finite configurations on the triangular lattice.
item.dc:creator: Till Rauch-M\"uller, Arsenii Sagdeev

item.title: Unilluminable rooms: minimal examples, classifications and exceptions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A room with mirrored walls can contain two points that are mutually invisible: no light ray from one reaches the other. Tokarsky built the first polygonal examples by tiling a room with reflected copies of a triangle and making every tile vertex of certain kinds a corner of the room. We study the smallest rooms of this kind, which we call lattice rooms. Their interior tile vertices of the remaining kind, the sources, are invisible and pairwise mutually invisible. On the tiling by isosceles right triangles, a hole-free lattice room with a source has at least 12 sides, attained only by the pinwheel. On the square tiling the least number is 16, again attained by one room. A hole-free lattice room with two sources has at least 24 sides on the first tiling and 34 on the square tiling. Up to congruence there are 12 such rooms with 24 sides, 89 with 25 sides and 14 with 34 sides. One absorbing post, one partition, or one hole that touches the outer boundary at one point lowers the least number of sides for two sources to 18, 20 and 22 (21 if sides are counted as maximal straight segments). Two and three posts give 17 and 16 sides, and a hole that does not touch the outer boundary gives 26. We list all smallest rooms. Rooms assembled from n modules have exactly 12n sides and n sources, and a hole-free lattice room with three or more sources has at least 36 sides. We also give rooms in which some tile vertices need not be corners: 15 types of 27-sided rooms on the tiling by triangles with angles 30, 60 and 90 degrees, which are smallest in their class, a nonagon with three mutually invisible corners, and a 42-sided room in which a rotation through 180 degrees takes the place of a corner. In a ring of three trapezoids a light ray returns to a corner that is invisible in one trapezoid. Several classifications rely on exhaustive computer searches made finite by the bounds proved here.
item.dc:creator: J. C. F. de Winter, George W. Tokarsky

item.title: Stabilization of the zero forcing number of generalized Petersen graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph $P(n,k)$ is $2k+2$ whenever $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We prove this by showing that the zero forcing number of the infinite generalized Petersen graph $P(\infty,k)$ is $2k+2$ and bounding the width of the closure of every set of at most $2k+1$ vertices. This bound gives a threshold on $n$ beyond which the projection of such a closure onto $P(n,k)$ does not wrap around. Combined with an exhaustive computer search for smaller $n$, we determine the zero forcing number of every $P(n,k)$ for $k\le 5$.
item.dc:creator: Young H. Kim, Youngsoo Kim, Byunghoon Lee

item.title: Properties of the Dichromatic Polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2611.13273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The chromatic polynomial is a well-studied function of graphs whose coefficients, factorization, and other properties are well-known to encode structural information about the underlying graph. An analogous notion of graph colouring exists for directed graphs which is also well-studied, but little is yet known about the corresponding dichromatic polynomial. We investigate properties of the dichromatic polynomial, including its coefficient interpretations, root-dense regions, and asymptotic growth. We also show that chordal digraphs' polynomials split into linear factors in a way analogous to the undirected case, confirm a conjecture on dichromatic uniqueness posed by Gonz\'alez-Moreno et al., and study the density of dichromatic polynomials within certain larger families of polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Lila Crew, Benjamin Keller, Katharina Kuehr, Shao Yuan Lin, Megan Ixchel Monroy Rodr\'iguez, Tabitha Williams

item.title: On the Chromatic Number of Cayley Tables of Dihedral Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A coloring of a Latin square $L$ is an assignment of $k$ colors to its cells such that no two cells sharing a row, a column, or a symbol receive the same color. The smallest $k$ for which such a coloring exists is called the \emph{chromatic number} of $L$, denoted by $\chi(L)$. The Cayley table of a finite group $G$ of order $n$ is a Latin square, which we denote by $L_G$. It is known that $\chi(L_G)\ne n+1$, so either $\chi(L_G)=n$ or $\chi(L_G)\ge n+2$. Moreover, $\chi(L_G)=n$ if and only if every Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$ is trivial or non-cyclic, which completely characterizes the finite groups whose Cayley tables attain the lower bound $n$. In this paper, we consider the dihedral group $D_n$ of order $2n$, where $n$ is odd. Since $D_n$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, it follows that $\chi(L_{D_n})\ge 2n+2$. We prove that this bound is sharp, that is, $\chi(L_{D_n})=2n+2$.
item.dc:creator: Kianoosh Shokri, Masoomeh Akbari

item.title: Positive Codegree Density of Suspensions of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the exact positive codegree density of suspensions of graphs $S^r(G)$ when $\chi(G)=t$ and $t-2$ is prime power. The value is $\gamma^+(S^{r}(G)) = \frac{(t-3)(t-2)^{r-1}}{(t-2)^r-1}$. The case of suspensions of $K_4$ gives the positive codegree density of daisies, answering a question of Balogh, Halfpap, Lidick\'y and Palmer. The lower bound construction is from Ellis, Ivan and Leader, while we establish the corresponding upper bound based on a weighted graph inequality.
item.dc:creator: Haiwen Luo

item.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.
item.dc:creator: Shin Hong, Jeongsoo Kim, Eunjeong Lee

item.title: Edge-coloring spectra of odd-fold graph covers and counterexamples to a conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.13394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a loopless multigraph $G$ and an odd integer $\ell\ge3$, let $\Delta(G)$ be the maximum degree of $G$, let $s_\ell(G)$ be the minimum chromatic index of a cyclic $\ell$-fold cover of $G$, and let \begin{align*} L_\ell(G):=\max\left\{ \Delta(G),\ \max_{\substack{S\subseteq V(G)\\ |S|\ge3\text{ odd}}} \left\lceil\frac{2\ell|E(G[S])|}{\ell|S|-1}\right\rceil \right\}. \end{align*} In this paper, we prove the sharp upper bound \begin{align*} s_\ell(G)\le\max\{\Delta(G)+1,L_\ell(G)\}. \end{align*} For every nonempty bridgeless cubic graph $H$, we construct two $3\ell$-regular graphs, one a multigraph and the other a simple graph. In each case, the minimum chromatic indices over cyclic and over all $\ell$-fold covers both equal the chromatic index of the multigraph obtained by replacing each edge of $H$ with $\ell$ parallel edges. Taking $H$ to be the Petersen graph gives both multigraph and simple graph counterexamples to a conjecture of Chen, van der Holst, Luo, and Ma, which asserts that $s_\ell(G)=L_\ell(G)$ always holds. When $G$ is connected and $L_\ell(G)>\Delta(G)$, we determine the common spectrum of its connected cyclic and arbitrary $\ell$-fold covers. We give polynomial-time algorithms to compute $L_\ell(G)$ and the spectrum endpoints. For fixed $\ell$, we also construct in polynomial time a connected cyclic cover with any prescribed chromatic index in the spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Runze Wang

item.title: Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order
item.description: arXiv:2611.13415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is vertex-transitive if, for any two vertices, there is an automorphism mapping one to the other. We prove that every connected vertex-transitive graph of order $p^n$, where $p$ is a prime and $p^n\geq 3$, has a hamiltonian cycle. Our main tool extends Witte's theorem [JCTB (1986)] on Cayley digraphs of $p$-groups.
item.dc:creator: Farzad Maghsoudi, Dragan Maru\v{s}i\v{c}, Bobby Miraftab

item.title: The Isomorphism Problem for Cayley Graphs on Monogenic Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the structural properties of Cayley graphs of monogenic semigroups and present a complete characterization of their weakly connected components. Several essential properties of these components are rigorously proven. Building upon these structural results, we introduce the notion of labelled colour-permuting isomorphisms between Cayley graphs. Using this new isomorphism framework, we address the Cayley graph isomorphism problem for monogenic semigroups, commonly known as the CI problem. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which two Cayley graphs over monogenic semigroups are labelled colour-permuting isomorphic.
item.dc:creator: Lu Li, Yong Shao, Lingli Zeng

item.title: Claw-free minimal bricks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $G$ is called a \emph{brick} if it is $3$-connected and $G-\{u,v\}$ has a perfect matching for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)$. A brick is \emph{minimal} if deleting any edge results in a graph that is no longer a brick. A graph is \emph{claw-free} if it contains no induced $K_{1,3}$. Plummer proved that every $3$-connected claw-free graph of even order is a brick. In this paper, we completely characterize all claw-free minimal bricks. Apart from $K_4$ and the six-vertex wheel $W_5$, they are precisely the line graphs of graphs obtained from loopless $3$-edge-connected cubic multigraphs by subdividing every edge outside a matching of even size exactly once. Consequently, every claw-free minimal brick of order $n$ contains at least $4n/5$ cubic vertices and at least $4n/5$ edges joining cubic vertices. Both bounds are sharp. This establishes the conjectures of Norine and Thomas and of Lov\'asz for claw-free minimal bricks in sharp quantitative forms. We also show that, for a claw-free minimal brick of order at least $8$, deleting an edge leaves a matching covered graph if and only if the edge lies in a triangle.
item.dc:creator: Guantao Chen, Yuying Ma

item.title: Divisibility graphs of semigroups as weighted poset blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a structural theory of divisibility graphs of arbitrary semigroups. For a semigroup $S$, let $S/{\mathcal J}$ be the poset of Green's ${\mathcal J}$-classes ordered by inclusion of principal ideals,and equip each $\mathcal {J}$-class $J$ with the weight $|J|$. We prove that the divisibility graph ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is obtained from the comparability directed graph $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ by replacing each $\mathcal J$-class with a complete symmetric graph of order $|J|$ and by replacing each directed edge $J_u$ to $J_v$ in $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ with all directed edges from every element of $J_u$ to every element of $J_v$. Consequently, ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is determined, up to isomorphism, by the weighted poset $(S/\mathcal {J},\{ J \}_{J\in S/{\mathcal J}})$. This yields structural descriptions of its strongly connected components, maximal unilaterally connected subgraphs. The main contribution is the reduction of divisibility graph problems to weighted quotient-poset problems. As applications, we obtain reconstruction and isomorphism criteria and prove an inheritance theorem for divisibility $D$-saturated subsemigroups.
item.dc:creator: Xuang Yang, Yong Shao, Lingli Zeng

item.title: Log-Concavity in Narayana Transforms and Stack-Sorting Fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a permutation $\pi$ of size $n$, let $D_\pi(x)$ denote the descent polynomial of the fiber of $\pi$ under West's stack-sorting map. We prove that $D_\pi(x)$ is ultra-log-concave of order $n-1$ and, therefore, log-concave. More generally, we prove that a multivariate refinement of $D_\pi(x)$ recording ascent tops and descent tops is the basis generating polynomial of a laminar matroid. We deduce a result about simplex integration from Br\"and\'en and Huh's theory and apply it to weighted matchings, obtaining a refinement of the log-concavity of $D_\pi(x)$ that incorporates the peak statistic on the stack-sorting fiber of $\pi$. These results imply the log-concavity of certain sums of products of Narayana polynomials over the lattice points of integral binary nestohedra. A complementary argument shows that replacing the monomials of a homogeneous real-stable polynomial with nonnegative coefficients by products of shifted Narayana polynomials produces a real-rooted polynomial; we discuss several applications. The results in this paper were formalized in Lean by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Colin Defant

item.title: The Largest Ground Set for Sunflower-Free Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.13495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct the largest $r$-flower-free system of $k$-uniform sets for $k=3, r=4$ where every element of the ground set $G$ is used at least once. The goal is to maximize $|G|$, also called the span. We define $\mathrm{sp}(k, r)$ to be the maximum $|G|$ for such a system. We show that $\mathrm{sp}(3, 4) = 39$, which yields an improved upper bound $f(3, 4) \leq 130$, improving upon the Erd\H{o}s--Rado bound of $f(3, 4) \leq 162$.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Wood

item.title: Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{T}_d$ be the triangular lattice with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ the set $\mathcal{T}_d$ can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors, a question left open by Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol for $2-\sqrt3\le d<2/\sqrt{37}$ and on several gaps between their constructions. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points of $\mathcal{T}_d$ in a closed unit disk, we show that $\mathcal{T}_d$ cannot be covered whenever $\mathcal{N}(d)<4/d^2$, and we determine this set of spacings exactly as a union of fifteen intervals; combined with their constructions, this shows that coverability is not monotone in $d$. At the right endpoints $d=2/\sqrt k$ of these intervals the density bound is attained, and we show that such a spacing is coverable if and only if $k$ is the norm of an Eisenstein integer. We also give two new coverings, at $d=1/\sqrt{13}$ and $d=2/\sqrt{21}$, in which the disks form a hexagonal packing. Consequently, together with an earlier result of Okayama, Kiyomi and Uehara, the smallest coverable spacing $d_{\min}$ exists and satisfies $2/\sqrt{55}<d_{\min}\le1/\sqrt{13}$, which answers a question of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol.
item.dc:creator: Teeradej Kittipassorn, Nattawut Phetmak, Kirati Sriamorn

item.title: The minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in graphs with no proper $k$-coloring
item.description: arXiv:2611.13580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider an integer $k\geq 3$. Toft and Tuza observed that every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has a cycle of length $0$ modulo $k$. Brewster, McGuinness, Moore, and Noel conjectured the following quantitative strengthening: every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has at least $\frac{(k+1)!}{2k}$ cycles whose lengths are divisible by $k$. The conjecture is sharp, as demonstrated by the complete graph on $k+1$ vertices. Kim and Picollelli confirmed the conjecture for $k=3$. We establish the conjecture for every $k\geq 3$. In other words, we determine the minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in a graph with no proper $k$-coloring.
item.dc:creator: Ilkyoo Choi, Kamil Sieniawski

item.title: Maximal Triply Even Binary Codes from Elliptic Orthogonal Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite set $X$, a binary linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^X$ is called a triply even binary code if $\operatorname{wt}(c)\equiv 0\pmod{8}$ for every $c\in C$. Let $q$ be an odd prime power and $n$ be an integer with $n\ge 2$. Let $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ denote the binary code spanned by all pairwise sums of rows of the adjacency matrix of the elliptic orthogonal graph arising from a $(2n+2)$-dimensional elliptic quadratic space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ is a triply even binary code if and only if $n=2$ and $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. In this case, we also prove that $E^-_6(q)$ is a maximal triply even binary code.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Kasai, Yuto Nogata

item.title: Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)
item.description: arXiv:2611.13593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general method, in finite cyclic groups, for constructing nonnegative rational functions $f$, normalized by $f(0)=1$, that satisfy the Coven-Meyerowitz condition $(T1)$ but fail $(T2)$, such that $f$ is a weak complement for a set tile $A$. Motivated by the unsupported-divisor questions in arXiv:2507.11672, we show that if a set tile $A$ admits an unsupported divisor, then a suitable dilation of $A$ admits such a rational weak complement $f$. Using this method, we construct an explicit example in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{180}$. The weak complements in our explicit perturbative constructions are not positive definite because of restrictions on the Fourier support of the perturbations. Thus these constructions do not resolve the proposed extension of the Coven-Meyerowitz conditions to positive-definite weak tilings (arXiv:2411.03854, Problem 1.2).
item.dc:creator: Gergely Kiss, Caleb Marshall, M\'at\'e Matolcsi, G\'abor Somlai

item.title: Triangles without a common vertex
item.description: arXiv:2611.13608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, $t(G)$ triangles, and adjacency spectral radius $\lambda(G)>\sqrt m$. Li, Feng and Peng (2025) conjectured that $t(G)\ge\sqrt m-O(1)$ if no vertex belongs to every triangle of $G$. We prove the stronger bound $t(G)\ge\lambda(G)-C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and give an explicit choice of $C$. The proof bounds the sum of the squared adjacency eigenvalues other than the largest and smallest. Interlacing and matrix perturbation estimates then restrict the neighbourhood of a vertex corresponding to a largest entry of a Perron vector to two disjoint edges and isolated vertices. A weighted count of the triangles completes the proof.
item.dc:creator: Dongxiu Cai, Xiao-Dong Zhang

item.title: The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem for cycle lengths $3$ and $n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem asks for a factorization of the complete symmetric digraph $K_v^*$ into directed $2$-factors, each of which is isomorphic to one of two given directed $2$-factors. In its uniform version, one seeks a decomposition of $K_v^*$ into $r$ factors consisting of directed $m$-cycles and $s$ factors consisting of directed $n$-cycles, where $r+s=v-1$. Let $m=3$, and let $n \geq 5$ be odd and not divisible by $3$. We show that, for every such $n$, the problem reduces to four decompositions of order at most $12n$: factorizations of $K^*_{3n}$ and $K^*_{6n}$ with every admissible number of factors of each kind, and two factorizations of the complete symmetric equipartite digraph with four parts of size $3n$. We construct these decompositions for $n=7$, and thereby give a complete solution for $(m,n)=(3,7)$: the obvious necessary conditions are also sufficient, with the single exception of $(v,r,s)=(6,5,0)$.
item.dc:creator: Ugur Odabasi, Dan Roberts, Richard M. Low

item.title: Uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with large maximum degree
item.description: arXiv:2611.13656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $G$ is \textit{uniquely $H$-saturated} if it contains no copy of $H$ as a subgraph, but adding any edge to $G$ creates exactly one copy of $H$ in the resultant graph. In this paper, we consider the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs and characterize the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta\geq n-5$. We prove that if $G$ is a uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graph with universal vertex $x$, then $G-x$ is either a star or a Moore graph of diameter 2. The uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with maximum degrees $n-3$ and $n-5$ are $\overline{C_{7}}$ and $G_{10}$ in Figure 2, respectively. But there are no uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with maximum degree $n-2$ or $n-4$.
item.dc:creator: Yuying Li, Weiyuan Zhang, Kexiang Xu

item.title: Judicious $r$-partitions of $r$-uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bollob\'as and Thomason conjectured that every $r$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges admits an $r$-partition such that each class meets at least $rm/(2r-1)$ edges. In this paper, we establish a lower bound of $(11-\sqrt{13})m/18$ for every $r\ge 2$. This improves Haslegrave's bound $rm/(3r-4)$ for every $r\ge 8$.
item.dc:creator: Siwei Lin, Qinghou Zeng

item.title: An automated approach to structure theorems for minimally repetitive rich words
item.description: arXiv:2611.13676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work on repetitions in rich words has led to the intensive study of the family of infinite rich words $\{{\mathbf u}_d:d\geq 2\}$, where ${\mathbf u}_d$ is the fixed point of the morphism $\varphi_d:\Sigma_d^*\rightarrow \Sigma_d^*$ defined by $\varphi_d(i)=\tt{0}(i+1)$ for $i\in\{\tt{0},\ldots,d-2\}$ and $\varphi_d(d-1)=\tt{0}(d-1)(d-1)$. For $d=2$ and $d=3$, it is known that the repetition threshold for infinite $d$-ary rich words is equal to the asymptotic critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$. Moreover, the structure of ${\mathbf u}_{2d-1}$ underlies the structure of all ``minimally repetitive'' $d$-ary rich words: there is a real number $t_d>E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ such that every infinite $t_d$-power-free $d$-ary rich word contains the language of $\pi({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ for one of finitely many morphisms $\pi:\Sigma_{2d-1}^*\rightarrow \Sigma_d^*$. We conjecture that a similar situation holds for all $d\geq 2$, and prove this for the first unknown case $d=4$. To do this, we develop a new approach for proving such structure theorems. Two key new concepts are ``compatibility'' of return words to palindromes in recurrent rich words, and ``$t$-persistent repetitions''. They facilitate the automation of several aspects of the proofs which were previously done laboriously by hand. We first demonstrate our approach by giving a much shorter proof of the known structure theorem for infinite $\tfrac{16}{7}$-power-free ternary rich words. Then we prove a new structure theorem: every infinite $2.12$-power-free quaternary rich word contains the language of one of seven distinct words of the form $\pi({\mathbf u}_7)$, up to permutation of the letters. We prove that all seven words are rich and have critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_7)$, so the repetition threshold for quaternary rich words is $E^*({\mathbf u}_7)\doteq 2.1197196907$.
item.dc:creator: Lubom\'ira Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Lucas Mol, Edita Pelantov\'a

item.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.
item.dc:creator: Vedat Levi Alev, Shravas Rao

item.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.13698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1997, Alon and Kim proposed an asymptotic edge-coloring bound motivated by a bound on the number of edges in intersecting uniform hypergraphs. The Alon--Kim conjecture asserts that, for fixed integers $k\ge t\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every $k$-uniform multihypergraph $H$ in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most $t$ vertices satisfies $\chi'(H)\le(t-1+\frac{1}{t}+\varepsilon)\Delta(H)$ whenever $\Delta(H)$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove the Alon--Kim conjecture. Our method combines finite-dimensional convex optimization with probabilistic methods.
item.dc:creator: Chengshuo Qiao, Zhijun Lu, Huimin Song

item.title: Two Types of Cards in Kelly-Ulam Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.13728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the case in Kelly-Ulam conjecture where there are only two types of cards in deck. It was possible to prove that graphs with this property are uniquely reconstructed by their card deck.
item.dc:creator: Max Zinchenko

item.title: Beyond Frankl's conjecture: Maximum sum of sizes of cross-intersecting families with restricted conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be two families of subsets of $[n]$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are \emph{cross-intersecting} if $F \cap G \neq \emptyset$ for all $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and $G \in \mathcal{G}$. Let $n, k_1, k_2, m, r, t$ be positive integers satisfying $n > k_1 + k_2$. Suppose that $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k_1}$ and $\mathcal{G} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k_2}$ are two cross-intersecting families such that $\left\{F \in \binom{[n]}{k_1} : |F \cap [m]| \geq r\right\} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is $t$-intersecting. In this paper, we determine the maximum sum $|\mathcal{F}| + |\mathcal{G}|$ under these assumptions. By taking $k_1=k_2+t-1$, $m = k_2+t+s-1$ and $r=k_2+t-1$ for $s\ge 0$, our result recovers a conjecture of Frankl \cite{frankl2016new}, which was recently confirmed by Wu, Feng, and Li \cite{wu2025proof}. Further, we establish a complete characterization of all extremal families. Our approach extends the Ahlswede--Khachatrian generating set method to handle the simultaneous constraints of cross-intersection and $t$-intersection, subject to additional structural conditions.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Jia, Qing Xiang, Jimeng Xiao, Huajun Zhang

item.title: Optimal radio labelings for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.13813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a simple graph $G$, let $d(u,v)$ denote the distance between two vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$, and let $diam(G)$ denote the diameter of $G$. A radio labeling of $G$ is a mapping $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\geq diam(G) + 1 - d(u,v)$ holds for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in G$. The span of $f$ is the difference between the largest and smallest integers assigned by $f$, and the radio number $rn(G)$ is the minimum span taking over all radio labelings of $G$. Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and let $H$ denote the Heawood graph (see Figure-1). In this paper we determine the radio number for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph, and characterize all optimal radio labelings of $P_n \Box H$. Moreover, we show that the radio number of $P_n \Box H$ exceed the lower bound given for $rn(G)$ in [6], where $G$ is any graph, and that this gap is arbitrarily large.
item.dc:creator: Payal Vasoya, Miral Doshi, Devsi Bantva

item.title: Counting $K_4$-saturating non-edges in Nosal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A non-edge of a $K_4$-free graph is $K_4$-saturating if adding it creates a copy of $K_4$, and $f(G)$ counts these non-edges. Erd\H{o}s and Tuza showed that the minimum of $f$ over $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graphs jumps from zero to a quadratic quantity once the number of edges exceeds $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Balogh and Liu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 109 (2014)] determined the asymptotic size of this jump. In this paper, we study the jump phenomenon at Nosal's spectral threshold $\lambda(G)>\sqrt m$, where $\lambda (G)$ is the spectral radius and $m$ is the number of edges. This spectral threshold does not involve the order, and its boundary contains unbalanced graphs far below the Mantel threshold. We prove that every $K_4$-free graph $G$ with $\lambda(G)>\sqrt m$ satisfies $f(G)+ \frac{1}{2}q(G)> \frac{1}{9} \lambda(G)^2$, where $q(G)$ counts the vertices in triangles. The constant $\frac{1}{9}$ is best possible, and the triangle-free case of this inequality reduces to Nosal's theorem. Consequently, the minimum of $f$ over $K_4$-free graphs with $m$ edges jumps from $0$ to $\frac19m+O(\sqrt m\,)$ at the Nosal threshold, and the error order $\sqrt m$ is best possible. For large $\lambda(G)$, we also prove $f(G)>\frac19\lambda(G)^2-\frac13\lambda(G)$, and graphs on the boundary $\lambda(G)^2=m$ attain this value. In the extremal graphs, the three edges of every triangle have booksizes in the ratio $4:1:1$, so these graphs are different from those of Balogh and Liu. We also show that the spectral Mantel condition $\lambda(G)>\lambda(T_{n,2})$ forces asymptotically fewer $K_4$-saturating non-edges than the condition $e(G)>\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Our proof transfers the Balogh-Liu theorem through a weighted blow-up and replaces the choice of an extremal edge by a zero-sum comparison over all edges of a neighborhood.
item.dc:creator: Yongtao Li

item.title: A Second Order Extended Zarankiewicz Number for Biquadratic SOS Rank
item.description: arXiv:2611.13858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the \emph{second order extended Zarankiewicz number} $z_{2M}(m,n)$, obtained from the second order Zarankiewicz number $z_2(m,n)$ of L\"ofberg and Qi by relaxing the simplicity condition $(S)$ for the \emph{secondary halves} of 2-edges, while keeping the limited condition $|E_1|=z(m,n)$. We prove the hierarchy $$ BSR(m,n)\ge z_{2M}(m,n)\ge z_2(m,n)\ge z_{SL}(m,n)\ge z_{RL}(m,n)\ge z_{wL}(m,n)\ge z(m,n), $$ and show that $z_{2M}$ is not capped by the universal cell bound. We prove the counting bound $z_{2M}(m,n)\le mn-1$, and a sharper linear-in-$m$ bound for fixed $n$ obtained from orthogonality of coefficient vectors. We analyse how the recursive criterion $(RW3^{+})$ of L\"ofberg and Qi must be modified under $(S_M)$, prove soundness of the resulting $(RW3^{+}_M)$ for multiplicity-one sharing, and show that a signed sharing closure $(SC)$ can supplement but not replace it. We prove $$ z_{2M}(21,4)\ge 56>55=z_2(21,4). $$ The witness is an explicit $56$-edge $(S_M)$-admissible configuration, and its irreducibility is certified by a full-rank system of $2255$ linear equations in the $1540$ off-diagonal inner products. This reaches Marin's lower bound $BSR(21,4)\ge 56$.
item.dc:creator: Liqun Qi, Gaohang Yu

item.title: Congruences for Dedekind numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study congruence properties of Dedekind numbers $d_n$. Our approach relies on actions of $p$-subgroups of symmetric groups on posets of monotone functions and leads to the congruences $d_{10}\equiv 106\pmod{210}$, $d_{11}\equiv 117\pmod{210}$, and $d_{12}\equiv 12\pmod{30}$. In particular, $d_{11}$ is odd, confirming a claim stated by Yamamoto without a proof.
item.dc:creator: Bart{\l}omiej Pawelski, Andrzej Szepietowski, B{\l}a\.zej Szepietowski

item.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.
item.dc:creator: Jan Pavl\'ik

item.title: Switching reconstruction of signed graphs: net-degree and balance
item.description: arXiv:2611.13901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The switching reconstruction problem for $2$-edge-colored graphs, introduced by Bondy and Mercier, asks whether such a graph is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of the graphs obtained by exchanging the colors of the edges at each vertex; for complete underlying graphs it is the vertex-switching reconstruction problem of Stanley. We study this problem in the language of signed graphs, where the net-degree of a vertex and the notion of balance come naturally into play. We prove that a signed graph on $n\neq4$ vertices is reconstructible when its net-degrees are all positive, all negative or all zero, which generalizes the reconstructibility of regular graphs in Stanley's problem. For connected balanced signed graphs, whose switching reconstruction problem we show to be equivalent to that of connected graphs with a distinguished bipartition of the vertex set, we prove reconstructibility when the two parts of the bipartition differ in size by more than two, and when all net-degrees are non-negative.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Cavaleri, Alfredo Donno, Stefano Spessato

item.title: Rank Reversals in Efficient Vectors for Pairwise Comparisons
item.description: arXiv:2611.13958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Studied are the orders among alternatives given by efficient vectors for a reciprocal matrix A. The focus is upon: 1) existence of efficient vectors with a given order and 2) discrepancies between the ranking for a pair of alternatives resulting from an efficient vector and from the corresponding entry of A, called rank reversals. We use matrix intervals in which the consistent matrices built from efficient vectors lie. The existence of efficient vectors (or those from constituent convex subsets) with a rank reversal at a given position is characterized. The minimum number of rank reversals for a reciprocal matrix among all weight vectors is described and it is shown that there is an efficient vector that has this number of rank reversals. A way to construct such a vector is given. The order transitive and the uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices are shown to be, respectively, the matrices for which there is an efficient vector with no rank reversals and the matrices for which all efficient vectors have no rank reversals. The effects on rank reversals of addition and deletion of alternatives are also discussed. Using numerical experiments, the frequencies of rank reversals in certain formulaic weight vectors are given.
item.dc:creator: Susana Furtado, Charles Johnson

item.title: Triangle Factors in the Semi-Random Graph Process
item.description: arXiv:2611.13959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The semi-random graph process is a single player game which starts with an empty graph on $n$ vertices and in each round the player is offered a random vertex and connects it to a vertex selected according to some strategy $\mathcal{S}$. The goal is, in as few rounds as possible, to arrive at a graph that satisfies some graph property $\mathcal{P}$. The main contribution of this work is to show that there is a strategy $\mathcal{S}$ which creates a $K_3$-factor in at most $2.929329 \, n$ rounds w.h.p.
item.dc:creator: Olaf Parczyk, Eva Schinzel

item.title: On the minimum number of entries in a set of maximal mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.13961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In superimposed form, a set of $k\ge2$ mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares of order $n$ is said to be maximal if no additional $k$-tuple may be inserted into any empty cell without violating orthogonality or the Latin property. For $k=2$ and $n\ge 21$ it is shown that the minimum number of filled cells in such a square is $\lceil n^2/3 \rceil$. Likewise for $k=3$ and $n\ge 44$ the minimum number of filled cells is $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil$ or $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil+1$, depending on the residue of $n$ modulo 4. In each case it is shown that the extremal systems are essentially those produced by a construction presented in the paper. A similar result is obtained for all $k\ge4$ for minimal systems that have a certain balance property, and it is conjectured that for sufficiently large $n$, even without this balance property, the extremal systems always correspond to those produced by this construction.
item.dc:creator: Diane M. Donovan, Mike J. Grannell, Emine Sule Yazici

item.title: On $q$-Ary $t$-Designs from Codewords of Every Nonzero Weight in Linear Codes and Their Duals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper investigates when the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design and how to generalize the property to its dual code. We reduce the verification of this property to a prescribed range of low weights. Specifically, for MDS codes, we show that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at every nonzero weight is equivalent to that at any fixed nonzero weight. As an application, we prove that the codewords of every nonzero weight in a $[q+1,3,q-1]_q$ MDS code and its dual hold $q$-ary $2$-designs if and only if $q$ is even. We also establish a duality principle. When $t\le\min\{d,d^{\perp}\}$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design if and only if the same property holds for its dual code. We then investigate narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,\delta,1)}$ and their duals. For $q=2^m$ and $\delta=2^r$ with $1\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in these codes form $q$-ary $2$-designs. Furthermore, for $\delta=4$ and $q=2^{m}$ ($m\ge4$), we establish that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,4,1)}$ form a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $m$ is odd.
item.dc:creator: Xinghao Wu, Junling Zhou

item.title: Treewidth versus Hadwiger number: Graph classes with dominated balanced separators are quasi-linearly treewidth-Hadwiger bounded
item.description: arXiv:2611.14070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, the treewidth of a graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is bounded by a function of the size of a largest clique minor of the graph if and only if the class $\mathcal{G}$ excludes some planar graph as an induced minor. Campbell et al. (arXiv 2024) conjectured that such a bounding function can always be chosen to be linear. We verify this conjecture for several classes of graphs (including even-hole-free graphs) and show that if a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$ has dominated binary-weighted balanced separators, then the bounding function can be taken to be in ${O(h \log h)}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number. We say that $\mathcal{G}$ has dominated binary-weighted balanced separators if, for every ${G \in \mathcal{G}}$ and every $\mathsf{w} \colon V(G) \to \{0,1\}$, there is a set ${D \subseteq V(G)}$ of bounded size so that deleting the closed neighbourhood $N_G[D]$ of $D$ leaves each component with at most a fixed fraction of the total weight of $G$. Our result reduces the quasi-linear weakening of the conjecture of Campbell et al. to a conjecture of Gartland and Lokshtanov stating that every graph class excluding a planar graph as an induced minor admits dominated binary-weighted balanced separators.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Dallard, J. Pascal Gollin, Andrea Munaro

item.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory for Lines and Finite Configurations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical question in Euclidean Ramsey theory, posed by Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus, asks which finite configurations $X\subset\mathbb E^2$ must appear in blue under every red--blue coloring of the plane having no red pair of points distance one apart. For $m \ge 2$, let $\ell_m$ denote the line of $m$ points with consecutive points distance one apart. Tsaturian showed that $\ell_5$ is unavoidable; we improve this to $\ell_7$. Additionally, we show that in every three-coloring of the plane in which two colors contain no $\ell_2$, the third color must contain an $\ell_3$. To conclude our discussion on lines, we prove several related results on two-colorings of higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces where both colors avoid longer lines. Our methods also extend to other point configurations. In any two-coloring of the plane in which one color contains no $\ell_2$, we show that the other color must contain both a regular pentagon of side length one and a unit square together with its center. We also prove that every two-coloring of three-dimensional space contains either a monochromatic unit square or a monochromatic noncoplanar tetrahedron with four edges of length one and two of length $\sqrt{2}$. Our proofs combine Sz\'ekely's averaging inequalities for distance-avoiding sets with the Fourier-analytic and linear-programming methods of de Oliveira Filho and Vallentin, together with a theorem on rotation-invariant measures from OpenAI's recent work on the Hadwiger-Nelson problem.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Hoff, Gary Hu, Yumo Liu

item.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.14140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Kuhlmann, Timm Oertel, Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests and complete bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ and an integer $m\ge2$ dividing $e(G)$, where $e(G)$ denotes the number of edges of $G$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb Z_m)$ is the least $N$ such that every $\mathbb Z_m$-labeling of $E(K_N)$ contains a copy of $G$ whose edge labels sum to zero. Bialostocki and Dierker (1990) [4] conjectured that $R(F,\mathbb Z_{e(F)})/R(F,2)\to1$ uniformly over all forests $F$ as $e(F)\to\infty$, where $R(F,2)$ is the two-color Ramsey number, and Caro (1991) [9] conjectured that $R(tG,\mathbb Z_t)=t(|V(G)|+d)-d$ for $t\ge2$ disjoint copies of $G$, where $d=\operatorname{def}_t(G)$ is the defect. We disprove the first conjecture by an infinite family of trees. Building on the work of Caro and on his joint work with Provstgaard, we obtain infinitely many counterexamples to the second conjecture, and we determine the zero-sum Ramsey numbers of a class of graphs: for powers of two $q\ge2$ we characterize all $s,k\ge1$ satisfying $R(K_{s,kq},\mathbb Z_q)=s+kq$, and we prove $R(mK_{q,q},\mathbb Z_m)=2qm+m/\gcd(m,q)-1$ for every $m\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Linlin Wang, Guoqing Wang

item.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.14177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.
item.dc:creator: Donghyun Kim, Jaeseong Oh

item.title: Coxeter cubes on the graph associahedron and separable elements
item.description: arXiv:2611.14178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Coxeter cube is a Boolean lattice inside a finite Coxeter group $W$ such that every square is a Coxeter square in the sense of Dyer and Wang. A Coxeter cube of full dimension based at the identity, which we call a based cube, is the same as a partition of the positive roots into inversion sets with one simple root in each block. These partitions were studied by Dimitrov, Gigliotti, Ossip, Paquette and Wehlau under the name of fine decompositions, and by Hohlweg and Pons as partitions of $w_0$. We show that the based cubes of $W$ form a point configuration in the graph associahedron $K(\Gamma)$ of the Coxeter diagram $\Gamma$ of $W$. The vertices of $K(\Gamma)$ are the based cubes whose blocks are parabolic. Every other based cube lies in the interior of an edge or of a cubical face, and we count the based cubes on each edge using the Coxeter arrangement. We also characterize the elements of $W$ that occur as vertices of based cubes. For the cubes at the vertices of $K(\Gamma)$ these are exactly the separable elements of Gaetz and Gao, and for arbitrary based cubes they satisfy a similar condition.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Gimenez, SuHo Oh

item.title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.14194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, for every fixed proper minor-closed graph class $\mathcal{G}$ and every positive integer $n$, there exists a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1+o(1)}$ vertices and edges such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $U_n$. This result generalizes and unifies the results of Dujmovi\'c et al. (J. ACM 2021) on induced-universal graphs and the results of Esperet, Joret, and Morin (J. London Math. Soc. 2023) on sparse induced-universal graphs from planar graphs to all proper minor-closed graph classes. It simultaneously improves the previous bounds for the number of vertices in induced-universal graphs (previously $O(n^2)$ obtained as a corollary of a result of DeVos et al. (J. Comb. Theory, Ser. {B} 2004) and a result of Gavoille and Labourel (ESA 2007)) and the number of edges in subgraph-universal graphs (previously $O(n^{3/2})$ by Babai et al. (Theory and Practice of Combinatorics 1982)).
item.dc:creator: Vida Dujmovi\'c, Cyril Gavoille, Gwena\"el Joret, Piotr Micek, Pat Morin, David R. Wood

item.title: The zero-sum constant $\mathsf{s}_p^*$ and inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.14248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. We denote by $\mathsf{s}_{p}^{*}$ the smallest integer $l$ such that, out of any given $l$ integers coprime with $p$, one can select $p$ integers satisfying that the sum of the $p$ integers is a multiple of $p$, but not a multiple of $p^{2}$. It was conjectured that $\mathsf{s}_p^*=2p+1$. In this paper we prove this conjecture and solve the corresponding inverse problem. More precisely, we characterize all sequences of $2p$ integers coprime to $p$ in which every $p$-term subsequence with sum a multiple of $p$ also has sum a multiple of $p^2$.
item.dc:creator: Cong Lin

item.title: A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize almost symmetric numerical semigroups in terms of their associated Young diagrams, showing that almost symmetry is equivalent to a simple numerical identity relating the genus, the type, and the number of small elements, and also to a combinatorial condition on the hook lengths of the diagram. We then introduce a symmetrization procedure that associates with each almost symmetric numerical semigroup a symmetric numerical set. This yields a map from the set of almost symmetric numerical semigroups to the set of symmetric numerical sets. We also present experimental data on the image of this map and on the proportion of its elements that are numerical semigroups. The results show, in particular, that the map is far from injective and that its image contains many numerical sets that are not semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Delgado, Meral S\"uer, Mehmet Ye\c{s}il

item.title: Intermediate Growth and Rigidity in Primitive Circulant Spectral Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At prime graph orders, the complete nontrivial and primitive Fourier spectra of a circulant coincide. We show that this agreement conceals a strong algebraic separation when the graph order varies. For any nonempty finite jump set $S$, let $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ be the algebra of arithmetic functions obtained by evaluating symmetric power sums on the primitive spectrum, filtered by power-sum weight. Removing the common Euler-totient term gives a reduced, locally finite algebra $B_S$, and we prove a filtration-preserving isomorphism $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}\cong B_S[T_2]$. Thus $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ is non-Noetherian and has Krull dimension one. Its filtered dimensions satisfy $\exp(c_S\sqrt{D/\log D})\leq \rho_S^{\mathrm{prim}}(D) \leq\exp(C_S\sqrt D)$ for large $D$, and its associated-graded Hilbert series is nonrational. Despite agreement on every prime order, the primitive and full spectral evaluation algebras intersect only in $\mathbb{Q}$. More strongly, no nonconstant primitive spectral function is eventually quasirational on residue classes. We give an exact finite-matrix rank formula and determine the quotient obtained by restricting to integers with large prime factors.
item.dc:creator: Juan D. V\'elez, Carlos A. Cadavid

item.title: Flagged Grothendieck enumerators and ribbon decomposition determinants
item.description: arXiv:2611.14298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Hamel--Goulden-type ribbon decomposition determinantal formulas for a new class of symmetric functions called flagged Grothendieck enumerators. In particular, these functions generalize both canonical refined stable Grothendieck polynomials and their duals. The proof uses Talaska's formula via flows on planar lattice graphs with systems of paths and cycles.
item.dc:creator: Alibek Adilzhan, Damir Yeliussizov

item.title: Negative-Dimensional Simplicial Complexes via the Grothendieck Group of the Join Monoid
item.description: arXiv:2611.14300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a framework that extends classical combinatorial and topological notions of simplicial complexes to a setting that includes simplicial complexes of negative dimension. This is achieved by considering the Grothendieck group of the commutative monoid of finite simplicial complexes under the join operation, which provides formal inverses and allows negative-dimensional objects to be defined. Within this group we adapt standard invariants such as $f$- and $h$-vectors, their corresponding polynomials, and the Euler characteristic. The same construction naturally endows the Grothendieck group with an Alexandroff topology. We show that this space is universal for finite topological spaces, and consequently the associated ordered simplicial complex is universal within its class.
item.dc:creator: Pedro J. Chocano, L. Felipe Prieto-Mart\'inez

item.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $\Sigma_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle. We prove that the eventual global filtered dimension is $MD+\lfloor D/2\rfloor+1-M(M+1)-g(\Sigma_S)$. Restricting graph orders to $n\equiv a\pmod q$, for $q\mid M$, replaces the genus term by the number of gaps of $\Sigma_S$ in the class $-a\pmod q$; the class $a=0$ gives the genus of the quotient semigroup $\Sigma_S/q$. These formulas yield an inverse reconstruction theorem: the unrestricted dimensions determine $M$, and the dimensions in all classes modulo $M$ at one common stable degree determine the Ap\'ery set and hence $\Sigma_S$. We give effective thresholds, exact examples, and a finite-rank algorithm valid in every degree. Reconstruction of the semigroup need not identify the original jump set.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Velez Caicedo, Carlos A. Cadavid

item.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.14322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial. For a Schur polynomial in $n$ variables indexed by $\lambda$, we show that the logarithm of the capacity associated with any nonzero coefficient can be approximated to additive error $\epsilon$ in time polynomial in $n$, $|\lambda|$, and $\log(1/\epsilon)$. The analysis establishes an explicit bounded optimization region and efficient approximate first-order oracles, and handles boundary weights through a factorization into smaller Schur polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Leake, Zirou Zhang

item.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [F\"orster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$. As an application of planar quasi-$4$-trees, we show that planar graphs of treewidth at most $4$ have vertex arboricity at most $2$. That is, the vertex-set of every planar graph of treewidth at most $4$ can be partitioned into two sets that each induce a forest.
item.dc:creator: Laura Merker, Samuel Schneider, Torsten Ueckerdt

item.title: Tolerance complexes of chordal graphs and squarefree symbolic powers
item.description: arXiv:2611.14384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a simplicial complex $K$ and an integer $t\ge0$, the $t$-tolerance complex $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ consists of the sets that become faces of $K$ after deleting at most $t$ of their elements. Kim and Lew conjectured that if $K$ is $d$-Leray, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(\eta(d+1,t+1)-1)$-Leray (the Leray conjecture), and that if $K$ is $d$-collapsible, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(\eta(d+1,t+1)-1)$-collapsible (the collapsibility conjecture), where $\eta$ is the Erd\H{o}s--Gallai number. We prove the collapsibility conjecture for $d=1$ when $t\le3$ or $\dim K\le4$, and for all $t$ when $K$ is the clique complex of a subtree graph of a spider, a class of chordal graphs containing all interval and split graphs; in particular, it holds for nerves of finite families of intervals. For every $d$, we prove both conjectures when $K$ has at most $d+1$ facets, when $K$ has nonzero homology in its top dimension, and when the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $K$ is squarefree stable. The Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is the $(t+1)$-st squarefree symbolic power of that of $K$, so the Leray conjecture becomes a regularity bound. Using this, we prove the Leray conjecture for flag complexes when $t\le3$, and for all $t$ for independence complexes of bipartite and chordal graphs, and we show that it is preserved under joins. We also construct chordal graphs $H$ for which the Leray number of $\mathcal{T}_t(\mathrm{Cl}(H))$ exceeds its Helly dimension by an arbitrarily large amount, and others for which it depends on the field. Finally, we reduce the case $t=1$ of the Leray bound for $d$-collapsible complexes to a question on intersections of links.
item.dc:creator: S Selvaraja

item.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
item.description: arXiv:2611.14430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.
item.dc:creator: Jes\'us F. Espinoza, Mart\'in Eduardo Fr\'ias-Armenta, Rosal\'ia G. Hern\'andez-Amador, H\'ector A. Hern\'andez-Hern\'andez

item.title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
item.description: arXiv:2611.14506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction. Second, we refute their log-concavity Conjecture 1: the same gap example violates log-concavity, and a further single-curve computation gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, which also fails log-concavity. Third, we establish the skew-shape block-statistic identity proposed in Kahane's Conjecture 4.4 (arXiv:2607.11225v1) for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, under an explicitly specified root-exclusion convention. Its proof combines commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations; the corresponding mathematical statements have Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. Fourth, we derive a bivariate block refinement whose coefficients are nonnegative after shifting the order parameter by one and, when necessary, multiplying by a monomial in the weight parameter. We specify the correction to the printed root convention, confirmed by Kahane in correspondence, and the geometric sign and specialization conventions clarified by the relevant authors for the annular examples.
item.dc:creator: Adam Til\`epe

item.title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula. The Gaussian degeneration recovers the $q$-deformed rationals of Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko. The regular and negative elliptic continued fractions agree, since they evaluate the same word with the same ordered weights. The numerator and denominator satisfy weighted Farey recursions and, for rationals greater than $1$, are the closure polynomials, or quiver $F$-polynomials, of the associated oriented type-$A$ quivers. Finally, we express the vertex weights as normalized elliptic Euler expressions of balanced virtual torus representations.
item.dc:creator: Shintarou Yanagida

item.title: Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps in Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $2r+1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces $S_{2r+1}^r$ through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For $r=1$, we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect. For $r=2$, subdividing one triangle of the Yuan--Stillman configuration gives a twelve-triangle family with fixed local direction counts; its dimension increases by one precisely on an open line segment. For every $r\ge3$, we construct a family with $2r+12$ triangles and fixed local direction counts, proving geometric dependence at degree $2r+1$. The moving vertex lies in an open triangle, and the dimension exceeds Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on its symmetry axis. The lower collinear vertices may have arbitrary strictly ordered heights. The low-order proofs use exact cofactor elimination. For higher orders, weighted interpolation and block elimination bound the global defect by one, and explicit extension and obstruction arguments determine the exceptional set.
item.dc:creator: Yi Zheng, Jiansong Deng, Xinyu Wu

item.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Yangcheng Li, Pingzhi Yuan

item.title: Combinatorial optimization with bounded subdeterminants
item.description: arXiv:2611.13065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $\Delta$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $\Delta$. For every fixed $\Delta$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $\Delta$-modular. We extend this list by showing that the same holds for many other problems, including the weighted versions of maximum cut, the traveling salesman problem, feedback vertex set, odd cycle transversal, dominating set, max 2-sat, induced matching, and cluster vertex deletion, as well as for $k$-colorability and graph isomorphism. Our proofs reveal several new ways in which bounded subdeterminants impose combinatorial structure: they bound the size or maximum degree of the input graph, bound packings of cycles and other obstructions, or yield decompositions into tractable graph classes such as forests, chordal graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, and graphs of bounded linear mim-width.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Fiorini, J. Pascal Gollin, Tony Huynh, Simon Keil, O-joung Kwon, Sang-il Oum, Roohani Sharma, Stefan Weltge

item.title: Constant query LCCs over the reals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This note describes a new construction, found by ChatGPT Astra, of constant query Locally Correctable Codes (LCCs) over the real numbers. Prior constructions of constant query LCCs were exclusive to fields of positive characteristic and were conjectured not to exist over the reals. The construction uses low degree polynomial evaluations over an integer grid, together with a novel sampling procedure which outputs, for a given grid point $P$, a random quadratic curve through $P$ which intersects the grid in many other points (the decoding queries). The sampler is `smooth' in the sense that no grid point is queried with high probability. These codes have the additional property that the queried locations (the curve/grid intersections) are all nearby grid points.
item.dc:creator: Zeev Dvir

item.title: Coordinatizing coalition lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.13353v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $P$ denote a finite poset in which no two incomparable elements have an upper bound. The coalition lattice Coal$(P)$ of $P$ consists of all subsets of $P$, ordered as follows: $X$ is less than or equal to $Y$ if and only if there exists an injective map from $X$ to $Y$ that sends each element to an element greater than or equal to itself. The main result coordinatizes Coal$(P)$ with integer vectors. With the help of this coordinatization, the paper gives new and shorter proofs of several results on coalition lattices proved by G. Cz\'edli, Gy. Poll\'ak, and B. Larose about three decades ago. As the main application of the coordinatization, the paper proves that if $K$ is a finite simple lattice with at least three elements, then Coal$(P)$ has no sublattice isomorphic to $K$. Previously, this was known only for $K=M_3$, by a result from 1996.
item.dc:creator: G\'abor Cz\'edli, Eszter K. Horv\'ath

item.title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.13390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any given uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, we show that every $\kappa$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_{\kappa}\star1$ (the $\kappa$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $\kappa$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Max Pitz, Lucas Real, Roman Schaut

item.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings
item.description: arXiv:2611.13585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Seb\H{o} and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected. This approach gives a $\frac{13}{10}$-approximation algorithm for $4$-regular $4$-vertex-connected graphs, improving the $\frac43$ of Newman, and a $\frac43$-approximation for $k$-vertex-connected graphs of maximum degree at most $k+1$, for every $k\ge 3$. For the general graphic TSP, we construct a feasible point in the odd-join polytope, using an optimal vertex from the Subtour linear programming relaxation of TSP, which helps us bound the approximation factor by 89/64.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gupta, Mehrdad Sohrabi, Levent Tun\c{c}el

item.title: A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.13848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F=\F_{2^n}$ and let \[ \mathcal T_1=\{t\in F:\Tr_{F/\F_2}(t)=1\}. \] For an integer $u=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_i2^i$ of even binary weight, put \[ L_u(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_iX^{2^i}, \qquad L_{1,u}(t)=t+L_u(t^{-1}). \] Hollmann and Xiang conjectured that $L_{1,u}$ permutes $\mathcal T_1$ if and only if $u\in\{0,3,6,10\}$. We prove the necessity by a moment method; the sufficiency is their Theorem~4.1. The quadratic moment yields a cyclic autocorrelation identity, while the cubic moment gives a two-variable group-algebra identity. An elimination argument reduces the coefficient word to a monomial or a complementary monomial, and explicit cubic and quartic moments complete the classification. We also prove Hollmann and Xiang's Conjecture~4.5. Namely, if $n>3$ and \[ L_{c,d}(x)=L_c(x)+L_d(x^{-1}) \] is a Kloosterman polynomial on $\F_{2^n}$, then its positive linearized part $L_c$ is injective on both trace fibers. This second result follows from relative quadratic and cubic moment identities and a spectral-zero rigidity argument. Consequently every Kloosterman polynomial is obtained by composing one of $L_{1,0},L_{1,3},L_{1,6},L_{1,10}$ with a linearized map that is injective on both trace fibers.
item.dc:creator: Yi Li

item.title: Feedback Vertex Set, Max Cut, and Edge Coloring on the Strong Product of a Graph and a Path
item.description: arXiv:2611.13917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine the computational complexity of well-known problems on subgraphs of the strong product of two paths. Namely, for Max Cut we show NP-hardness on induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ answering a question by Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Huynh, Joret, Liu, and Wood (2021). For 3-Edge Coloring we show NP-hardness on subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ and that it is equivalent to 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs for induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$. It is a long standing open question whether 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs is NP-hard. As a second contribution, we consider graphs of the form $G \boxtimes P$ and show that Feedback Vertex Set on these graphs is FPT in the clique-width of $G$. Furthermore, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is chordal or co-comparable and that the computational complexity depends on the parity of $P$ if $G$ is bipartite. Namely, it is solvable in polynomial time if $P$ has an even number of vertices but is NP-complete otherwise. For Max Cut, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is bipartite.
item.dc:creator: Jan Diester, Kolja K\"uhn, Manuel Rapp, Samuel Schneider, Torsten Ueckerdt

item.title: Sharp Proximity Bounds for Integer Programs with Few Rows
item.description: arXiv:2611.14052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the proximity between an optimal vertex of a standard form linear program with constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ and an optimal integer solution. When $m = 2$, we prove the sharp infinity-norm bound $\Delta-1$, where $\Delta$ is the largest absolute maximal minor of $A$. When $m = 1$, we express the difference between an optimal LP vertex and an optimal integer solution as a nonnegative combination of certain generators in the kernel of $A$ with a bounded coefficient sum. This implies sharp proximity bounds for all norms when $m=1$. Combining this representation with its known counterpart for Hilbert bases due to Sissokho, we develop techniques that transfer results from $m=1$ to $m=2$. Along the way, for $m=2$, we prove that such a representation exists for an extended Gomory group relaxation and obtain the sharp infinity-norm bound $\Delta$ for Graver basis elements. We also present a new short proof of Sissokho's result and lower bounds on the proximity for all $m$ and $\Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Kuhlmann, Luze Xu

item.title: Gorenstein dimensions for stable Auslander algebras of Nakayama algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A$ be a Nakayama algebra and $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ its stable Auslander algebra. We introduce a new homological invariant, called the finitistic Gorenstein dimension, which coincides with the classical Gorenstein dimension whenever the latter is finite, and compute this invariant for $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ when $A$ has infinite global dimension. Combined with an accompanying criterion for the finiteness of the Gorenstein dimension of $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$, our results provide a complete description of this dimension and verify the Gorenstein Symmetry Conjecture for this class of algebras. Furthermore, we show that the finitistic Gorenstein dimension of $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $ is also left-right symmetric, is explicitly related to the finitistic dimension of $A$, and can be attained among the injective dimensions of the projective $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $-modules corresponding to simple $A$-modules.
