Our proofs rely on computing injective dimensions in terms of distances in the coresolution forest of $A$, a combinatorial structure closely related to Ringel's coresolution quiver.
item.dc:creator: Odysseas Giatagantzidis, Carolin Hartung, Nupur Jain, Ren\'e Marczinzik, Martin Rubey, Sven Schmitz

item.title: Affine Springer fibers, Cherednik algebra modules and Hilbert schemes: torus link case
item.description: arXiv:2611.14190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a pair of positive integers $M,N$ with GCD $d$, we relate the bigraded $S_N\times S_d$-Frobenius characters of the homology of the positive part of a homogeneous affine Springer fiber for $\mathrm{GL}_N$ of slope $M/N$ to a direct sum of the associated graded of minimal supported modules of type $A_{N-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra at the same slope, and to the equivariant K-theory of a coherent sheaf on the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. For the first object, we use the Hessenberg paving of Goresky-Kottwitz-Macpherson; for the second and third objects, we resort to an explicit Hodge module on $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. The bridge between them is a non-coprime shuffle theorem of Kim-Oh.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Thomas Hameister, Xinchun Ma

item.title: The Monophonic Directed Convexities
item.description: arXiv:2611.14191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph Convexity is a topic with many papers in the literature, especially on the $P_3$, geodesic, and monophonic convexities in undirected graphs. Regarding directed graphs, Erd{\H o}s et al. in 1972 and Chartrand and Zhang in 2000 obtained the first results on the $P_3$ and geodesic convexities for directed graphs, respectively. In this paper, we start the investigation of monophonic convexity on directed graphs. We define two convexities, the monophonic and the strong monophonic directed convexities, related to the minimal and the induced directed paths, respectively. We show that deciding whether a set is convex is polynomial-time solvable in the monophonic convexity, but coNP-complete in the strong monophonic convexity. For both convexities, we prove that the hull number is NP-complete even in DAGs. Regarding the monophonic convexity, we prove that the hull number is polynomial time solvable in tournaments, but the interval number is NP-complete in tournaments and also in bipartite oriented graphs.
item.dc:creator: J\'ulio Ara\'ujo, Ana Karolinna Maia, Thiago Marcilon, Nicolas Nisse, Rudini M. Sampaio

item.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.
item.dc:creator: Jan Pavl\'ik

item.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.14367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: K\"uhnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.
item.dc:creator: Geunho Lim

item.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
item.description: arXiv:2611.14471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Defrain, Corentin Jazeron, Kazuhisa Makino

item.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.14475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.
item.dc:creator: Christian K\"ummerle, Dustin G. Mixon

item.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2611.14513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1. A new lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms. 2. A new upper bound of $O(n (\log \log n)^2 / \log^2 n)$ for randomized algorithms. 3. A new upper bound of $O(n / (\log \log n)^{2-\varepsilon})$ for deterministic algorithms for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For randomized algorithms, we nearly close the gap between the lower and upper bounds; the remaining gap is only $O((\log \log n)^2)$. We establish the asymptotic separation between randomized and deterministic online graph coloring. Against an oblivious adversary, a polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio asymptotically smaller than any deterministic algorithm can guarantee, even with unlimited computation.
item.dc:creator: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda

item.title: Around Sperner's lemma
item.description: arXiv:1405.7513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sperner's lemma guarantees a triangle with three different labels. How many such triangles must there be? We begin with the familiar proof by doors and rooms and show that orienting the doors gives an exact signed count. The boundary labeling then provides a lower bound even when the region has holes. With more than three labels, a small geometric construction supplies an additional factor: a boundary that winds $w$ times around a cycle of $n$ labels forces at least $(n-2)|w|$ colorful triangles. We connect the count to Brouwer's fixed point theorem and elementary winding arguments, derive a quantitative version of Tucker's lemma, and conclude with a higher-dimensional glimpse in which the Hopf invariant forces nine tetrahedra.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R Musin

item.title: Torus Queen Independence
item.description: arXiv:2404.18237v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Define a queen on $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ with admissible moves parallel to $\mathbf{x}\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$ at arbitrary length. How many queens can be placed on $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ without any two in conflict? In 1918, P\'{o}lya showed that $n$ queens on $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$ cannot be conflict-free if $n$ is a multiple of $2$ or $3$. We conjecture and partially prove that no $n^{d-1}$ queens on $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ are conflict-free if $n$ is divisible by a prime less than $2^d$. On the other hand, extending work by Monsky from 1989, we show there are $(n-c)n^{d-2}$ conflict-free queens on $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ for some constant $c=c(d)$.
item.dc:creator: Kada Williams

item.title: Berge Pancyclic hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2410.21733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An $n$-vertex graph $G$ is {\em pancyclic} if for every $\ell$, $3\leq \ell \leq n$, $G$ contains a cycle of length $\ell$. We consider an analog for hypergraphs. An $r$-uniform hypergraph is a set of vertices and a set of edges in which every edge contains $r$ vertices. A Berge cycle of length $\ell$ in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of $\ell$ distinct vertices and $\ell$ distinct edges $v_1,e_1,v_2, \ldots, v_\ell, e_{\ell},v_1$ such that $\{v_i, v_{i+1}\} \subseteq e_i$ for all $i$, with indices taken modulo $\ell$. We similarly call a hypergraph {\em Berge pancyclic} if it contains Berge cycles of every possible length. For sufficiently large $n$ we prove a sharp minimum degree condition guaranteeing Berge pancyclicity in $r$-uniform hypergraphs where $3 \leq r \leq \lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor - 2$. This bound is optimal for all such combinations of $n$ and $r$.
item.dc:creator: Teegan Bailey, Yupei Li, Ruth Luo

item.title: On Scarf's theorem for Generalized Cooperative Games
item.description: arXiv:2501.05802v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study a generalization of cooperative games with non-transferable utility. Our model is motivated by Shapley's proof of Scarf's theorem, which revealed a deep connection between KKM-type theorems and cooperative games. In recent decades, further developments have established deeper connections between algebraic topology and combinatorial KKM-type fixed-point theorems. We explore the consequences of these developments for cooperative game theory. In our model, coalitions are replaced by firms, each represented by a resource vector and a set of feasible payoff vectors in a common payoff space. We define the core and fractional core for these games and relate their nonemptiness to homotopy invariants of covers associated with the game. Consequently, we obtain a Scarf-type theorem for generalized cooperative games. This framework allows us to model cooperative games with threats and political games.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail V. Bludov, Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Abelian and Dihedral equiangular tight frames of redundancy $2$
item.description: arXiv:2509.01753v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies group frames ($G$-frames) where the unitary group representation can be projective. When the group is abelian, for most combinations $N, n$, we show that $ETF(N,n)$ can only exist for genuinely projective group representations. In particular, cyclic-group frames for such parameters do not exist. We also give a characterization of all dihedral tight frames and dihedral $ETF(2n,n)$, using which, we conclude that regular dihedral $ETF(2n,n)$ must be genuinely projective. Following that, we give a characterization of regular dihedral $ETF(2n,n)$ in terms of certain structured skew Hadamard matrices. We then show that Paley $ETF(2n,n)$ and its doubling are both of this type. Finally, we classify all regular dihedral $ETF(2n,n)$ for $n\le 22$ up to switching equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Radel Ben Av, Xuemei Chen, Assaf Goldberger, Kasso A. Okoudjou

item.title: Characteristic quasi-polynomials of deletions of Shi arrangements of type C and type D
item.description: arXiv:2509.02043v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characteristic quasi-polynomials enumerate the number of points in the complement of hyperplane arrangements modulo positive integers. In this paper, we compute the characteristic quasi-polynomials of the restrictions of the Shi arrangements of type C and type D by one given hyperplane, respectively. The case of type C is established by extending the method developed in our previous work on type B (\cite{HN2024}), while the case of type D is deduced through a direct connection with the results on type B. As a corollary, we determine whether period collapse occurs in the characteristic quasi-polynomials of the deletions of the Shi arrangements of type C and type D. Moreover, it turns out that the intersection posets of the Shi arrangements of type B and type C are not isomorphic as posets if their rank is at least $3$.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Higashitani, Masato Konoike, Norihiro Nakashima, Satoshi Ono

item.title: On a Question of Mirzakhani and Vondr\'ak concerning Sperner Labelings of the Simplex-Lattice Hypergraph
item.description: arXiv:2511.03036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mirzakhani and Vondr\'ak asked whether the simplex-lattice hypergraph admits a Sperner-admissible labeling in which every hyperedge receives at most two colors. We answer this question affirmatively by introducing the \emph{dominant labeling}, in which every lattice point is labeled by its unique \emph{dominant index}. In their hybrid model of fair division, this yields preference functions under which at most two players are nearly satisfied. We determine the number of vertices of each color and the number of hyperedges using a given pair of colors; these counts are expressed through the entries of Catalan's triangle. We also characterize the color sets of hyperedges of the other hypergraphs that arise from the edgewise triangulation of the dilations of the standard unit simplex.
item.dc:creator: Ognjen Papaz, Du\v{s}ko Joji\'c

item.title: Sufficient average degree conditions for the existence of large highly connected subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.08256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mader proved that every sufficiently large graph with average degree at least $(2+\sqrt{2})k-1$ has a $(k+1)$-connected subgraph. He also conjectured that already an average degree of at least $3k-1$ is sufficient. The best known sufficient factor was improved by multiple authors but never reached $3$. In the present paper, it is further improved to $3.109$. In addition, the obtained $(k+1)$-connected subgraph is guaranteed to have more than $1.2k$ vertices. Moreover, similar conditions on the average degree are proven to be sufficient for the existence of even greater $(k+1)$-connected subgraphs. In particular, for $\sigma\geq \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$, every graph with average degree at least $\big(2+\sigma+\frac{1}{3\sigma}\big)k-1$ has a $(k+1)$-connected subgraph on more than $(1+\sigma)k$ vertices, where the factor $2+\sigma+\frac{1}{3\sigma}$ is asymptotically sharp for $\sigma \geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Krone

item.title: Partial sequencings and other combinatorial aspects of large groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.19285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A \emph{partial sequencing} of length $k$ in a finite group $G$ is a sequence $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{k-1}$ of distinct elements of $G$ with $g_0=1_G$ such that the partial products $g_0,\, g_0g_1,\,\dots,\, g_0g_1\cdots g_{k-1}$ are also distinct. Partial R-sequencings and partial harmonious sequences are defined similarly. Using the recent work of M\"uyesser and Pokrovskiy, we determine when such partial sequences extend to full ones in sufficiently large groups. In particular, if $G$ is sufficiently large and $k\le\sqrt{|G|}$, then a partial sequencing of length $k$ extends to a sequencing of $G$ if and only if some element of $G$ that is not one of its partial products has the same image in the abelianization as the product of all elements of $G$. This holds automatically when the commutator subgroup has more than $k$ elements, and we show that it can fail otherwise. Using the fact that every group of odd order has a symmetric harmonious sequence, we also prove that $\mathbb{Z}_{2^k}\times H$ is doubly R-sequenceable for every group $H$ of odd order, unless it is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ (in particular, every abelian group other than $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is), that $K\times H$ is symmetric sequenceable whenever $K$ is, that all sufficiently large groups are doubly sequenceable, doubly R-sequenceable, doubly harmonious and doubly $\#$-harmonious, and we verify these four properties for all groups of order $4$ to $12$ and for several small dihedral and dicyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Solution of Erd\H{o}s Problem 633
item.description: arXiv:2604.03609v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify triangles that can be tiled only into a square number of congruent triangles, settling Erd\H{o}s Problem 633.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson, Miklos Laczkovich, Yan X. Zhang

item.title: Higher Rank-Support Weights and q-Polymatroids
item.description: arXiv:2605.23284v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a $(q,m)$-polymatroidal approach to higher supports and higher rank-weight enumerators of rank-metric codes. In this framework, we establish analogs of several fundamental results known for matroids and linear codes, including the description of minimal supports in terms of cocircuits of truncations and a Greene-type identity relating higher rank-weight enumerators to rank generating functions. We also show that the associated $(q,m)$-polymatroid and the higher support distributions determine each other. As a further application, we derive MacWilliams-type identities for higher rank-weight enumerators.
item.dc:creator: Koji Imamura, Shinya Kawabuchi, Keisuke Shiromoto

item.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2605.23291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple. As a corollary, for a random $K\times N$ matrix over a finite field with i.i.d.\ rows, uniform sampling from the nonzero vectors maximizes the probability of full row rank. Finally, we show that uniform sampling maximizes $\Prob\big(\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)\ge r\big)$, and hence also $\E\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$, for every $L, r$.
item.dc:creator: Mladen Kova\v{c}evi\'c

item.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
item.description: arXiv:2606.18048v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Koml\'os, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemer\'edi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\log\Delta/\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfies: $$\chi_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstra\"ete and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo

item.title: 3-Neighbor bootstrap percolation on two-dimensional grids
item.description: arXiv:2608.06133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the $3$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process, a vertex becomes (and remains) infected if at least three of its neighbors are infected. We say that an initial configuration of infected vertices percolates if eventually all vertices are infected. We exactly determine the size of the minimum percolating set for the $3$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on all remaining open cases for rectangular grid graphs $P_m\square P_n$. This extends earlier work of Dukes, Noel, and Romer.
item.dc:creator: Neal Bushaw, Alexander Clifton

item.title: An AFLT-type generalization of the $q$-Baker--Forrester ex-conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.05836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Habsieger--Kadell $q$-Morris constant term identity, which is equivalent to the famous $q$-Selberg integral, has been generalized in numerous ways since the 1980s. Among these, there are two important generalizations: (i) the $q$-Baker--Forrester ex-conjecture, which was conjectured by Baker and Forrester in 1998 and proved by K\'{a}rolyi, Nagy, Petrov and Volkov in 2015; (ii) the AFLT-type $q$-Morris identity (equivalently, the AFLT-type $q$-Selberg integral), which was obtained by Albion, Rains and Warnaar in 2021, as a $q$-analog of the result of Alba, Fateev, Litvinov and Tarnopolskiy (AFLT). In this paper, by the Gessel--Xin method and the Macdonald polynomials with prescribed symmetry, we unify these two generalizations.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Zihao Huang, Wenlong Jiang, Yue Zhou

item.title: The crossing number and the unit-distance crossing number of the Hamming graphs H(d,3)=K_3^{box d}, and their realizations over many coordinate fields
item.description: arXiv:2609.13757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hamming graph H(d,3)=K_3^{box d} (n=3^d vertices) is the graph of single-symbol errors of ternary codes. Can it be drawn in the plane with every edge one unit long and no two non-adjacent vertices a unit apart? It can, for every d, joining two problems into one. Arithmetic: over which coordinate fields is it realizable? As a Minkowski sum of unit triangles (planar for the whole family only in base 3), each H(d,3) has not one faithful realization but a (d-1)-parameter continuum, whose field climbs the constructibility hierarchy (ruler-and-compass, origami, and beyond); yet almost every realization is transcendental, in no number field, matching the exists-R hardness of unit-distance recognition. Combinatorial: beside the ordinary crossing number cr we introduce the unit-distance crossing number udcr(G), the fewest crossings over faithful unit drawings (every edge a unit segment); it is the rectilinear crossing number under unit length, so cr <= rcr <= udcr. We prove cr(H(d,3))=Theta(n^2) (one-page 7/6 n^2 above; spectral bisection Omega(n^2) below) and cr <= 2/3 n^2 via a two-page book layout; and udcr(H(3,3))=231 exactly, with udcr(H(d,3))=O(n^2 log n). A structure theorem makes every faithful planar realization a Minkowski sum, so the realization variety is an explicit (d-1)-parameter flex containing the udcr optimum; the matching udcr=Omega(n^2 log n) is the central open problem. The invariants differ: for cr the crossing-minimal drawings are structurally opaque, whereas the udcr optimum is itself a faithful Minkowski realization. All claims are verified in exact arithmetic with reproducible code and figures.
item.dc:creator: Haroldo Costa Silva Filho

item.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.11047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum asserts that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, that is, for almost all graphs $G$, every graph with the same spectrum as $G$ whose complement has the same spectrum as the complement of $G$ is isomorphic to $G$. We prove this conjecture by showing that the random graph $G(n,1/2)$ is determined by its generalized spectrum with probability tending to one. The proof combines a local theory of the denominators of the rational orthogonal matrices that relate generalized cospectral graphs, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, Seidel switching, inverse Littlewood--Offord theory over finite fields, rank estimates for random symmetric matrices modulo primes, and a study of the rational factors of the characteristic polynomial of a random symmetric $\pm1$ matrix with zero diagonal.
item.dc:creator: Ziqing Xiang

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number by an arbitrarily large amount
item.description: arXiv:2611.03236v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Rubin and Taylor asked whether $(a,b)$-choosability implies $(am,bm)$-choosability for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni disproved this for $(a,b,m)=(4,1,2)$ and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. Following an earlier discussion by Jiang and Zhu, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G)\le\mathrm{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$, where $\mathrm{ch}(G)$ is its choice number and $\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G)$ is its strong fractional choice number, defined as the infimum of the real numbers $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$. In this paper, we prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph of choice number three that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. This answers the question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni affirmatively and the other questions negatively, even for planar graphs. Next, for all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, we construct a graph of choice number $k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable, using only the six-vertex wheel $W_5$ as its core gadget. The case $t=0$ and $b=2$ recovers the result of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni. The supremum of $\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G)-\mathrm{ch}(G)$ is at least $1/7$ over planar graphs of choice number three, and at least $1/3$ over graphs of choice number $k$ for each $k\ge4$. Finally, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\mathrm{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(2k+t,2)$-choosable, where $t\ge C\sqrt{k}$ for an absolute constant $C>0$. Thus the gap is unbounded even with multiplicity fixed at two. We further obtain $k+\Omega(\sqrt{k})\le\sup\{\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G):\mathrm{ch}(G)=k\}\le2^{(1+o(1))k}$ as $k$ tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Yangyan Gu, Rongxing Xu

item.title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
item.description:
arXiv:2611.11128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $
u(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and let $	au(G)$ be the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. We prove $	au(G)\le2
u(G)$ when each edge belongs to at most four triangles, the edges belonging to four triangles form components with at most two edges, and the maximum average degree is at most $25/2$. No upper bound on maximum vertex degree is imposed. We also localize the density condition. Let $K$ be the Hifumi core, defined as the vertex set of the 4-core of the spanning subgraph formed by edges belonging to at least three triangles. It suffices to impose the density condition on $G[K]$, including all original edges between vertices of $K$. More generally, when the four-triangle edges have maximum degree at most two, reductions produce a subgraph $R\subseteq G[K]$ with $	au(G)-2
u(G)\le	au(R)-2
u(R)$. Consequently an empty core gives a density-free sufficient condition. For the first graph class, a quantitative surplus argument strengthens both the global and localized density conditions to the strict bound $25/2+2/56775$. The proof combines edge reductions, discharging, finite certificates and a weak K"onig--Egerv'ary lemma for links of arbitrary order. The general conjecture and the removal of the density condition from the first graph class remain unresolved here.
item.dc:creator: Yasuhito Tsujimura

item.title: Independence number and odd dominating models
item.description: arXiv:2611.11205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A dominating $K_t$-model, introduced by Illingworth and Wood [J. Graph Theory, 2025], is a sequence $(T_1,\dots,T_t)$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint subtrees of $G$ such that every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour in $T_i$ for $1\leq i<j\leq t$. Let $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. We prove two dominating-model analogues of improvements to the classical Duchet-Meyniel bound [Ann. Discrete Math., 1982]. The first extends a result of Kawarabayashi, Plummer, and Toft [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2005]. Every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)\geq2$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)\geq(n+\omega(G))/(2\alpha(G)-1)$. Second, we prove a constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound for dominating models: every graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)>0.51075n/\alpha(G)$. This qualitatively extends the results of Fox [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2010] and Balogh and Kostochka [Discrete Math., 2011]. An odd dominating $K_t$-model is a dominating $K_t$-model with an assignment of one of two colours to each vertex of $V(T_1)\cup\dots\cup V(T_t)$, such that every edge of each $T_i$ is bichromatic and, for $1\leq i<j\leq t$, some edge between $T_i$ and $T_j$ is monochromatic. Let $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. Our constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound relies on our next result: every claw-free graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)\geq 2\chi(G)/3$, generalising a result of Chudnovsky and Fradkin [J. Graph Theory, 2010]. The factor 2/3 is best possible [arXiv:2512.20392]. For $t\geq2$, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with no odd dominating $K_t$-model has independence number at least $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$. For the stronger notion in which every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour of the same colour in $T_i$, we prove the analogous results with $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$ replaced by $(n+t-1)/(3t-3)$.
item.dc:creator: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, David R. Wood, Jung Hon Yip

item.title: R-harmonious groups
item.description: arXiv:2512.08830v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A finite group $G$ of order $n$ is \emph{R-harmonious} if the non-identity elements of $G$ can be listed as $g_1,g_2,\dots,g_{n-1}$ so that the consecutive products $g_1g_2,g_2g_3,\dots,g_{n-1}g_1$ again list every non-identity element exactly once. Beals, Gallian, Headley and Jungreis proved that an abelian group is R-harmonious if and only if it does not have a unique element of order~$2$ and is not $\mathbb{Z}_3$. We prove a lifting lemma which shows that, under suitable conditions on $G/H$, a group $G$ with a normal subgroup $H$ of odd order is R-harmonious. As applications we show that every group of odd order whose abelianization is not an elementary abelian $3$-group is R-harmonious; in particular, every nontrivial group of odd order not divisible by~$3$ is R-harmonious. We also show that every split extension of a group of odd order by a ``harmoniously matched'' group is harmoniously matched, and hence R-harmonious. Together with a computer search, this gives many non-abelian even-order R-harmonious groups, among them the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ with $n\equiv 8\pmod{16}$ or $n\equiv 16\pmod{32}$. Finally, we observe that the quaternion group $Q_8$ satisfies the Hall--Paige condition but is not R-harmonious.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: A Dynamic Survey of Soft Set Theory and Its Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2602.21268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Soft set theory provides a systematic framework for parameterized decision-making by associating each parameter with a subset of a given universe, thereby enabling structured representations of uncertainty [1, 2]. Over the past decades, the theory has evolved into a broad range of extensions, including hypersoft sets, superhypersoft sets, TreeSoft sets, bipolar soft sets, and dynamic soft sets, while also establishing connections with various mathematical disciplines, particularly topology and matroid theory. This book presents a comprehensive survey of soft set theory and its principal extensions, with particular emphasis on parameter spaces, value spaces, representative mathematical constructions, and the underlying assumptions necessary for rigorous comparisons among different frameworks. It carefully distinguishes established definitions from the literature from exploratory formulations and critically examines the limitations of selected claims concerning representation and reduction. Building upon the first edition, this second edition introduces additional concepts and illustrative examples, addresses previously identified mathematical inconsistencies and typographical errors, and refines the overall structure and presentation to enhance mathematical rigor, clarity, and readability.
item.dc:creator: Takaaki Fujita, Florentin Smarandache

item.title: Subperiodic groups and bounded automorphisms of periodic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.12630v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A subperiodic group is a group of motions of $d$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb R^d$ which contains a translation lattice $\mathbb Z^r$ of rank $r < d$ as a subgroup of finite index. Cayley graphs of subperiodic groups are used to illustrate the concept of bounded automorphisms (particularly of finite order), i.e. those when the distance between a graph vertex and its image has an upper bound. The description of subperiodic groups in dimension 3 in terms of subgroup structure and abstract group isomorphism types [75 crystallographic rod groups ($r=1$) and 80 layer groups ($r=2$) belong to 32 and 34 types, respectively] allows for a convenient characterization of bounded automorphisms of their Cayley graphs. An easy-to-compute set of invariants is developed for recognizing the isomorphism types of crystallographic groups in $\mathbb R^3$ from finite presentations which makes use of only the number of nonconjugate subgroups up to a given finite index $n$ ($n \leq 12$ for rod groups, $n \leq 8$ for layer groups, and $n \leq 24$ for space groups), and how many of them are normal. A criterion is proven that if a finite (inverse-closed) generating set of a group $G$ is stabilized by conjugation by a nontrivial element of finite order in $G$, then the respective Cayley graph possesses nontrivial bounded automorphisms of finite order. This criterion is applied to three-periodic sphere-packing graphs. Subperiodic groups in $\mathbb R^4$ with a three-dimensional translation lattice are used to systematically derive embeddings of three-periodic ladder graphs in $\mathbb R^3$.
item.dc:creator: Igor A. Baburin

item.title: Temporal Cliques Admit Linear Spanners
item.description: arXiv:2606.05156v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A temporal graph is a graph in which every edge carries a non-empty set of time labels, and it is temporally connected if for every two vertices $u$ and $v$, there exists a $u$-$v$-path with non-decreasing time labels. A spanner is a subset of its edges preserving temporal connectivity. Unlike static graphs, temporally connected graphs need not admit sparse spanners; nonetheless, minimizing spanner size is a central and widely studied problem. A particularly intriguing question is whether temporal cliques admit spanners of linear size. Despite considerable effort over the past years, the best known upper bound remained $O(n \log n)$. We finally resolve this question, proving that every temporal clique on $n$ vertices admits a spanner of size $7n$. Moreover, such a spanner can be computed in polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Julia Baligacs

item.title: Multiway Partition is FPT for Connectivity Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.10380v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E$ be a set of $n$ elements, $f\colon2^E\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ be submodular, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in E$ be distinct, and $k\in\mathbb N$. The Submodular Multiway Partition problem asks whether $E$ has a partition $(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$ with $t_i\in P_i$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i f(P_i)\le k$. We prove that this problem can be solved in $r^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$ time whenever $f$ is posimodular. This covers monotone submodular functions, matroid rank functions, and nonnegative combinations of monotone and symmetric submodular functions. When $f$ is a connectivity function, we remove the dependence on the number of terminals and obtain a $k^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm. The proof is entirely elementary, and is arguably the simplest proof that Edge Multiway Cut is fixed-parameter tractable. As a new consequence, our main result immediately implies that Hypergraph Multiway Partition is fixed-parameter tractable.
item.dc:creator: Tony Huynh, Eun Jung Kim, Sang-il Oum, Roohani Sharma, Marek Soko\l{}owski

item.title: Square root crystals and the square root of $B(\infty)$
item.description: arXiv:2608.11009v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a general monoidal category of $\mathbf{N}$-root crystals and then study the special case of square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals. The latter objects include Yu's crystals on semistandard set-valued tableaux. Prior work of the first author, Tong, and Yu showed that regular square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals can be a useful tool for proving Grothendieck positivity results. The objects studied here go beyond the regular case and allow us to construct a square root analog of the direct limit crystal $B(\infty)$. We give several descriptions of our square root of $B(\infty)$, using marginally large tableaux, the Lusztig or PBW parameterization, and the Nakashima--Zelevinsky polyhedral model. We show that this crystal has a simple character formula, exhibits a nontrivial Demazure filtration, and recovers Yu's semistandard set-valued tableau crystals after taking appropriate tensor products. We also investigate a number of differences between square root crystals and classical crystal constructions.
item.dc:creator: Eric Marberg, Travis Scrimshaw

item.title: Binary Multiple-Node-Erasure-Correcting Codes over Complete Graphs: Constructions, q-Ary Metric Balls, and Duality
item.description: arXiv:2609.01474v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Codes over graphs store symbols on edges of a complete undirected graph on $n$ vertices with a self-loop at each vertex; erasing a node removes all its incident edges. Extending Yohananov, Efron, and Yaakobi's construction, we obtain binary codes correcting any three node erasures at infinitely many prime lengths $n$, unconditionally, with redundancy $3n-2$, one bit above the graph Singleton bound. The earlier construction has the same redundancy but requires $2$ to be primitive modulo $n$, which is not known for infinitely many primes. We give a deterministic decoder for these triple-node codes using $O(n^2)$ binary operations and construct Singleton-optimal binary triple-node codes at $n=6,8,10,12$. When $2$ is primitive modulo an odd prime $n$, we extend their double- and triple-node codes to binary codes correcting $\rho$ node erasures with redundancy $\rho n-(\rho-1)$ for $2\leq\rho\leq(n+1)/2$, saving $\rho-1$ bits over the binary symmetric rank-metric construction when $\rho<(n+1)/2$. Over every finite field of size $q$, the node weight of a word is the least number of vertices whose erasure removes its support. We give exact formulas for ball volumes in this node metric and prove that, for fixed $q,t$, the radius-$t$ volume is asymptotic to $\binom nt q^{tn-\binom t2}$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain existence and covering bounds; for fixed $q,\rho$, we show that linear $\rho$-node-erasure-correcting codes exist with redundancy at most $\rho\log_q n+O_{q,\rho}(1)$ above the graph Singleton bound. Finally, reformulating Yohananov and Yaakobi's criterion, we show that a linear code over any finite field is Singleton-optimal for $\rho$ node erasures if and only if its dual is Singleton-optimal for erasures of the coordinates inside any $n-\rho$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2609.13570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.
item.dc:creator: Samira Arfaee, Bryan Wong

item.title: An exact compress-with-another threshold in a binary automaton family
item.description: arXiv:2610.07044v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a state $q$ in a synchronizing automaton, let $\mu(q)$ be the minimum length of a word merging $q$ with another initial state. Szyku{\l}a asked whether $\mu(q)=O(n)$ for strongly connected synchronizing automata and described a binary family attributed to D\.{z}yga, with $n=3p$ states and a conjectured threshold $4n/3$. We specify the boundary transitions omitted from the published piecewise definition and prove that the resulting automata $\mathcal A_p$ satisfy $\mu(q_0)=4p=4n/3$ for all $p\geq3$. A shortest word merging $q_0$ with another state is $(ba)^p(ab)^p$. We also construct a reset word of length $3p^2+4p-1$. Consequently, any uniform linear upper bound for $\mu(q)$ on binary strongly connected synchronizing automata with corank-one letters has leading constant at least $4/3$.
item.dc:creator: Qichao Wang, Daoyu Dong

item.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.22622v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Badger

item.title: Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities
item.description: arXiv:2610.36638v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplus\Lambda^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko, Artem Lopatin

item.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
item.description: arXiv:2610.39941v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang, Charles E. Hughes
